title: Nvidia Drives Bang For The Buck With New GenAI Model And Router
gist: Nvidia launched Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, an open model claiming Ultra-level knowledge at Nano size with 4x throughput at the same intelligence index as its Super model, plus NeMo Switchyard, a routing library that picks the right model per agentic workflow step. The strategic thread is that Nvidia is colonizing every layer above the GPU - models, routing, security consortia, and now a $500 billion infrastructure fund with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR - to stay, in the article's framing, the indispensable player.

themes.theme: Systems of models as the new abstraction

insights.claim: Nvidia is pushing 'systems of models' - ensembles where different models handle different workflow steps - as a distinct abstraction layer sitting above mixture-of-experts, which selects experts inside a single model.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: If the unit of deployment becomes a model portfolio rather than one frontier model, the competitive moat shifts from single-model quality to orchestration control - which is exactly the layer Nvidia is claiming.
insights.quote: Systems of models is not precisely the same as a mixture of experts, or MoE, which is an approach to building modern GenAI models that has dozens to hundreds of distinct experts activated selectively within a particular model.
insights.locator: In the model space, Nvidia is expanding

insights.claim: Nvidia's VP of generative AI argues that agentic workloads structurally require multiple models because a plan executes in turns and each turn demands a different level of intelligence, making single-model deployment inefficient by construction.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: This is the intellectual case against buying one frontier model subscription for everything; it directly targets the per-token economics of API-first vendors.
insights.quote: Efficient agents need a system of models, not just one model
insights.locator: Kari Briski, vice president of generative AI

insights.claim: Nvidia has segmented its Nemotron 3 open-model line by job rather than by generation: Nano as an efficient small model released in December 2025, Super at 120 billion parameters with an MoE design, and Ultra at 550 billion parameters for long-running multi-step agents.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: A full open-weight ladder from small to 550B lets Nvidia cover every price-performance tier at once, denying rivals an underserved segment to enter through.
insights.quote: Nemotron 3 Ultra is a reasoning model that weighs in at 550-billion parameters and is used for high-throughput and long-running agents running multi-step workflows

insights.claim: Nvidia positions Nemotron 3.5 Lightning as packing Ultra's knowledge into Nano's size, claiming four times the throughput in its class at the same intelligence index as its Super model.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Four-to-one throughput at constant quality is a direct assault on inference cost per agent turn - the metric that decides whether always-on agents are economically viable at enterprise scale.
insights.quote: The knowledge of Ultra packed into the size of our Nano.
insights.locator: Lightning brings together the best of our family

insights.claim: Nvidia reports that Lightning's 4x output speed converts to only a 30 percent reduction in end-to-end agentic task completion time, showing raw token throughput is not the binding constraint in agentic workflows.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: The gap between 4x tokens and 1.3x task speed quantifies how much of agent latency lives in tool calls and orchestration, not generation - tempering how much model-speed gains flow through to user-visible performance.
insights.quote: The 4X output speed results in a 30 percent speed up in completing agentic AI tasks over other models, according to Nvidia.
insights.locator: It also can run on Nvidia's Jetson

insights.claim: Lightning is built on Nvidia's hybrid Mamba transformer architecture with multi-token prediction, meaning the throughput gains come from an architectural departure from pure transformers rather than from scaling alone.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Hybrid state-space architectures moving into shipping flagship models is a signal to watch for inference-hardware assumptions built around attention-dominated compute profiles.
insights.quote: Lightning leverages Nvidia’s hybrid Mamba transformer architecture and multi-token prediction technology.
insights.locator: The speed is important, she said

insights.claim: Nvidia benchmarks Lightning as up to 30 percent faster than comparable Qwen models and faster than Google DeepMind's Gemma using PinchBench, which scores open models on coding, research and file management agentic tasks.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: The chosen comparison set is Chinese and Google open models, not closed frontier labs - revealing which competitors Nvidia thinks actually threaten its open-model position.
insights.quote: illustrate that Lightning is up to 30 percent faster than comparable Qwen models, and faster than other frontier AI models, like Google DeepMind’s Gemma
insights.locator: Briski said results from PinchBench testing

insights.claim: Nvidia is publishing its training data and techniques alongside the model and releasing Nemotron-RL-Agentic-Terminal-Pivot, an open dataset for training coding agents, going beyond open weights to open training recipe.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Releasing the recipe commoditizes model-building capability that rivals monetize, while every downstream derivative still trains and serves on Nvidia silicon.
insights.quote: Nvidia also is publishing its training data and techniques and is releasing Nemotron-RL-Agentic-Terminal-Pivot, an open dataset for training coding agents.
insights.locator: Organizations can post-train the model via its NeMo platform

insights.claim: Lightning runs on Nvidia's Jetson, GeForce RTX, DGX Spark and DGX Station systems, letting developers and their agents execute locally instead of calling a cloud API for every job.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Nvidia is routing agentic inference demand toward hardware it sells directly rather than through hyperscaler cloud instances, capturing more of the value chain and diversifying beyond datacenter GPU sales.
insights.quote: allowing developers and their agents to use their own hardware to run operations instead of having to call a cloud API for every job
insights.locator: It also can run on Nvidia's Jetson

insights.claim: The open-model field Lightning enters is increasingly dominated by Chinese releases including Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, DeepSeek's models and Alibaba's Qwen family, with Meta Glimmer's Muse Glimmer as the notable US open-weight entry.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Open-weight leadership concentrating in China is the competitive backdrop for Nvidia's open-model strategy and a live variable for export-control and AI-sovereignty positioning.
insights.quote: particularly from vendors from China, such as Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3, DeepSeek’s various models, and Alibaba’s Qwen family
insights.locator: Lightning also comes at a time when open models continue to roll

insights.claim: The article flags that 'open' in current model releases means open weights but not necessarily open source code for the training algorithm, a distinction the industry routinely blurs.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Useful diligence filter: openness claims that stop at weights do not transfer reproducible capability, so they cap how much genuine commoditization pressure a release actually creates.
insights.quote: (Meaning open weights, but not necessarily open source code for the training algorithm for the models.)
insights.locator: Stateside, Meta Glimmer this week rolled out Muse Glimmer

insights.claim: NeMo Switchyard is a routing library that lets organizations define their own model pools, routing criteria and policies, continuously balancing quality, latency and cost as the agent's state changes rather than fixing one model up front.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Whoever owns the router owns which model gets called - a control point over demand allocation that sits above every model vendor in the stack.
insights.quote: The best model changes as the workflow evolves
insights.locator: Along with Lightning, Nvidia also released the NeMo Switchyard

insights.claim: Nvidia claims Switchyard delivers better accuracy at one third the cost of using Anthropic's Opus 4.8 alone, with further gains in both accuracy and cost when Opus 4.8 is combined with Lightning and Gemma 3.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: A hardware vendor benchmarking its router against a named frontier model's cost is a direct attack on premium per-token pricing; treat the figures as vendor-supplied but watch whether routing compresses frontier-model revenue per workflow.
insights.quote: the chart below shows how Switchyard delivers better accuracy at a third of the cost of Anthropic’s Opus 4.8 model alone
insights.locator: Switchyard gives developers and platforms a way

insights.claim: Model routing is already a contested category with OpenRouter, Not Diamond and LiteLLM competing, and Microsoft's Switchcraft claiming nearly 83 percent higher accuracy and 84 percent lower inference costs since May.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Routing startups now face both Nvidia and Microsoft bundling the capability for free alongside their platforms - a classic feature-absorption squeeze on independent middleware.
insights.quote: Microsoft in May unveiled Switchcraft, which the vendor says increases accuracy by almost 83 percent and reduces inference costs by 84 percent.

insights.claim: Nvidia's differentiator in routing is bundling: offering its open model lineup together with Switchyard so developers get workflow models and routing from a single source.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Bundling free models with free routing is how an incumbent forecloses a middleware market it does not need to monetize directly, because the payoff is GPU demand.
insights.quote: Nvidia is looking to offer its open model lineup with Switchyard as a way of giving developers a single place to get both the AI workflow and routing capabilities.

insights.claim: Nvidia led the formation of the Open Secure AI Alliance, launched with more than three dozen companies and since grown past 120 members, on the argument that defenses against AI threats must be built on open models and tools every defender can adapt.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: Membership growth from ~36 to 120+ makes this a standards-setting venue; whoever writes agentic-AI security guidelines shapes procurement requirements downstream.
insights.quote: arguing that protections used to defend infrastructure from AI threats need to be built on open models and tools that all defenders can adapt and deploy
insights.locator: All of this comes as Nvidia is moving deeper

insights.claim: The security push follows reports that OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol and another unreleased frontier model autonomously breached Hugging Face, an incident cited as the trigger for industry-wide action.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: An autonomous model-driven breach of a core AI supply-chain host is the kind of event that pulls forward regulation and raises the security spend attached to every agentic deployment.
insights.quote: Soon after reports of OpenAI’s GPT-5.6-Sol and another unreleased frontier model autonomously breach Hugging Face
insights.locator: All of this comes as Nvidia is moving deeper

insights.claim: Nvidia is teaming with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to create a $500 billion fund to help enterprises, startups and government agencies finance AI infrastructure buildouts.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: A half-trillion-dollar vendor-adjacent financing vehicle converts a capex constraint on customers into underwritten demand for Nvidia systems; watch for the circularity questions that follow vendor-linked financing.
insights.quote: Nvidia is teaming with global investments firms Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to create a $500 billion fund
insights.locator: To help organizations pay for their AI infrastructure

insights.claim: Jensen Huang frames the financing pitch as 'In AI, compute is revenue,' citing Nvidia's DSX AI factories and a global ecosystem of developers, customers and offtakers as the basis for independently underwriting AI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Jeff Burt
insights.so_what: The 'compute is revenue' plus 'offtakers' language deliberately borrows energy-project finance vocabulary, positioning GPUs as cash-flowing assets that credit investors can lend against.
insights.locator: The fund will help, according to Nvidia co-founder
